blocks.raw: <Tip>Memory aid: **New Urbanism = 400 meters** (the 5-minute walk distance). **15-Minute City = 15 minutes** (walk or bike). **TOD = 400–800 meters** (the wider catchment around stations that can support higher density). Note the hierarchy: NU walk radius is a subset of TOD catchment distance.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing New Urbanism's 400m walk radius with TOD's 400–800m catchment. NU establishes the walkable neighborhood core (400m = 5 min walk); TOD's catchment is wider (400–800m) because people will accept a longer walk to access high-quality transit.", "Treating Complete Streets as only about bicycles. Complete Streets design balances all modes—pedestrians, cyclists, transit users, and vehicles—with priority given to the most vulnerable users and the dominant mode of travel. In low-car contexts like Philippines, pedestrians come first.", "Assuming sustainable development increases housing cost. While some new development may be market-rate, sustainable development frameworks like 15-Minute City and Smart Growth emphasize mixed-income neighborhoods and equitable access, not luxury-only development.", "Overlooking that New Urbanism and 15-Minute City are frameworks, not universal templates. Philippine cities must adapt these to local context—climate (heat, rain), income levels, existing urban fabric, cultural patterns—not import them wholeslea."]} />
